## Mario Archila

I am a clinician-scientist with a decade-long track record in medicine and neuroscience research. I combine neuroimaging, electrophysiology, machine learning, and computational modelling to answer neuroscientific questions, and I lead a {{< var group.focus >}} research program.

My primary focus is unravelling the neurophysiological underpinnings of cognition, and of language perception in particular, together with their implications for brain pathologies. A defining commitment of my research line is translational: turning fundamental research insights into tangible clinical and neurosurgical solutions.

## Research approach

I work at the frontier of functional neurosurgery, from deep brain stimulation and epilepsy surgery to electrocorticography (ECoG) and neuroprosthetics, integrating clinical innovation with rigorous research. Building on hands-on experience with ECoG, I draw on principles from physics (including chaos theory), network neuroscience, and artificial intelligence to pioneer new therapeutic approaches that both deepen our understanding of brain mechanisms and enhance patient care.

Delivering on this often means building the tools the science requires. I develop new acquisition and analysis methods, with an emphasis on optimising ultra high-field 7 Tesla functional and anatomical MRI sequences, for both applied research and clinical use.

A second thread runs alongside this clinical work: understanding both natural and artificial intelligence, and using AI to improve diagnostics and therapeutics. I see enormous potential for AI in science and believe that, done right, it can accelerate scientific discovery, particularly in healthcare. A fuller account of these questions and the methods behind them is on the [Research](research.qmd) page.

## Values & open science

I am committed to reproducible research: open software, documented pipelines, and clear data statements accompanying published work, within ethical and institutional constraints. I treat artificial intelligence as a tool to be used responsibly, in the conviction that, applied well, it can accelerate discovery and improve care.

## Collaboration

I care deeply about collaboration and am always eager to work with multidisciplinary teams that harness science and technology to advance patient care. I welcome connections with researchers and clinicians who share a collaborative vision for science and for the future of medicine, neuroscience, and AI and their real-world applications. You can see who I currently work with on the [Collaborations](collaborations.qmd) page, and reach me through the [Contact](contact.qmd) page.
